item.title: Some of the best Simply Smashed R&D still happens in my mum's back garden. Family BBQ a fe…
item.description:
Some of the best Simply Smashed R&D still happens in my mum's back garden.
Family BBQ a few weeks ago (rip summer, feels like it ended the second we packed the grill away) and half of it quietly turned into a taste test.
New patties on the grill, a couple of sauces we've been messing with, everyone chewing and giving their verdict whether you asked for it or not.
One of them was the New Yorker, a pastrami smash we'd been arguing over for weeks.
It's been selling out on repeat since.
This is genuinely how a lot of it still works. Not a lab, not a focus group.
A grill in the garden and a family that'll tell you straight when something's rubbish.
What's the best thing you've ever had off a family BBQ?

item.title: My parents landed in Dhaka and the whole neighbourhood called the police on them. Here is …
item.description:
My parents landed in Dhaka and the whole neighbourhood called the police on them.
Here is what my mother did next:
They flew out in the middle of March 2020, just as Bangladesh closed its borders to Europe. Anyone arriving from the UK had to quarantine for fourteen days.
A short trip turned into nearly seven weeks.
My parents did the fourteen days exactly as told. Their neighbours did not believe them.
They rang the police again and again to report that my parents had been seen outside.
They had not been outside once.
I was in London, twenty-one, doing what my generation does when it feels powerless. I tweeted about it. I tagged our MP, whose helpline for stranded nationals went to a mailbox nobody read.
Low-risk travellers were being flown out of Sylhet. My father, who was high risk, was told nothing at all.
None of it moved a single flight.
Then my mother rang with a story about a rickshaw puller. Someone had asked whether he was frightened of the virus.
He said the only thing he feared was an empty stomach for his family.
Ramadan came at the end of April. My parents were still stranded, still being reported by their own neighbours.
They spent it making food packs with whatever family was nearby and getting them out across the city.
Think about that for a moment.
They were the most vulnerable people on that street. And their answer to being treated as a threat was to go and feed people.
We have become very good at the visible response, the kind where you post about something and tag a politician. It feels like action and it feeds nobody.
They had no platform, so they served the person in front of them.
The Prophet (peace be upon Him) said the best of people are those most beneficial to people.
My parents landed back in London on the 3rd of May. My father came through arrivals in full PPE.
It was my twenty-second birthday.
Neither of them has mentioned those food packs since.
If your parents are still with you, ask them what they did in the year nobody was watching.
